title: AP-1 cargo read-back
summary: Take 32 archived designs to 128 clonal wells, mark each well so sequencing says which well it came from, and call a pass or a fail per well.

background.title: Which designs are read back
body: This run reads every design built from 2 fragments or more: 32 of 72. The rest stay polyclonal and are never read one design at a time.

Every design is spotted from AP-1 cargo archive plate, which this run reads a copy of and never changes. A design whose spot grows nothing has no clone to read, and is re-transformed before anyone re-synthesises it.

background.title: How a well is told from the rest
body: The index PCR route marks each well: amplify each well with one barcoded primer pair. The other route marks the same wells a different way, and the picking, the pass rule and the reformat are the same either way.

A well's marks are worked out from where the well is rather than looked up, so a demultiplexer can check an address instead of trusting a file. One axis of the address is the plate: this run pools 2 plates, and the marks tell 96 plates apart on one flow cell.
A well is called above 20 reads. The other route's floor is not a stricter or a looser setting of the same scale, so neither number carries over to the other route.

inputs.name: AP-1 cargo archive plate
inputs.what: one clonal stock a design, 72 of them, sealed and frozen

inputs.name: Barcoded index primer plate
inputs.what: the lab's index primer plate IDX-01, prepared once and called for by a run

protocols.title: Design read-back: index PCR
protocols.summary: Take 32 archived designs to 128 clonal wells, mark each well so sequencing says which well it came from, and call a pass or a fail per well.
highlights: A design is read back as a name and a count of the pieces it was built from, never as bases, so any clonal stock this lab holds can be read back here.
The bench is sized from the 32 designs read and not from the sheet, so a design the floor leaves out costs no well, no plate and no reagent.

materials.name: 384-well culture plate
materials.note: 60 µL low-salt LB with kanamycin a well

materials.name: 96-well half-skirted PCR plate
materials.amount: 2, one a quarter of a picked plate

materials.name: Barcoded index primer plate
materials.amount: 2 µL a well at 1 µM each, 96 forward and 96 reverse
materials.note: prepared once as lab stock, by its own protocol; a run calls for it. The SI's plate preparation ends at 0.1 µM, where its own protocol and the article both stamp 1 µM, which is what this takes

materials.name: Taq DNA Polymerase
materials.note: 5 U/µL, so one reaction takes 0.25 units

materials.name: DMSO, molecular biology grade
materials.amount: 0.4 µL a reaction, 4% (v/v) in the well

equipment: A sequencer, and a demultiplexer that can check an address

plates.name: picked 1
plates.holds: one picked colony each in 60 µL low-salt LB with kanamycin
plates.note: 128 of 384 wells picked, a quarter at a time

plates.name: index 1
plates.holds: one barcoded PCR each, the pair its own address names

plates.name: index 2
plates.holds: one barcoded PCR each, the pair its own address names

steps.title: Array 32 designs and grow
instructions: Spot each design from its archive plate as its own spot on a 25 cm BioAssay plate.
notes: This run reads back every design in 2 fragments or more: 32 designs. The rest stay polyclonal and are never read one design at a time.
The archive is untouched: this reads a copy of it.
expected: One spot a design, at about 2,500 colonies a plate, which is the density picking wants.

troubleshooting.solution: That design has no clone to read. Re-transform it from the archive before anyone re-synthesises it.

steps.title: Pick 4 colonies of each design
instructions: Pick 4 colonies a design into 60 µL low-salt LB with kanamycin, with the QPix XE Microbial Colony Picker.
Fill one quarter of each 384-well plate before starting the next.
notes: 4 colonies a design is Lund's anchor and the only measured one; four gave a clean copy of 343 of 458 genes.
A quarter at a time is what makes a part-filled plate give full plates downstream, and what keeps a mark off a plate that is mostly empty.
expected: Every colony of one design sits on one plate.

troubleshooting.problem: A design in many fragments gives no clean colony
troubleshooting.solution: The chances above say which designs that is likeliest for. Pick more colonies of those designs before the plates are poured, not after.

steps.title: Sample the picked plates into index plates
instructions: Move 1 µL of each well into its 96-well plate, one quarter of the picked plate a pass.
notes: One well in four lines up under a head built for the smaller format, so a quarter moves in one pass.

transfers.title: Sample a quarter of picked 1 into index 1
transfers.note: one well in four, which is the spacing a head built for the index format reads

transfers.title: Sample a quarter of picked 1 into index 2
transfers.note: one well in four, which is the spacing a head built for the index format reads

steps.title: Amplify each well with its own pair
instructions: Add 7 µL of the master mix below to each well, which already holds its 1 µL of culture.
Add 2 µL of the pair its address names from the lab's index primer plate IDX-01, for 10 µL a well.
Seal the plate, spin it down, and run the program below.
notes: 96 forward marks and 96 reverse reach 9,216 wells, so the pairs already held cover far more than this run needs.
The primer plate is built once as lab stock and a run calls for it; this protocol does not build one.
The first 10 cycles touch down from 68 to 63.5 °C, 0.5 °C a cycle, and 25 more run at 68 °C.
Extension is 2 minutes, what the authors ran for a gene below 1 kb. The published rule is at least one minute a kilobase, so a longer design wants it raised.
The mix is made 1.5 times what the wells take, which is what LevSeq's own per-plate table spells out. Nothing says what the surplus is for.

tables.title: Index PCR, one well a sample

expected: One barcoded amplicon a well. A well's own place in the plate names its forward mark — the first well the first mark — and every well of one plate takes that plate's own reverse mark.
One band a well, the design plus about 100 bp: the two marks, and the stretch between the primer sites and the reading frame.

troubleshooting.problem: A plate reads back far fewer wells than the others
troubleshooting.solution: LevSeq traces that to the amplification, not the sequencing: on a run of ten plates three returned under 60% of their variants. Check each pool on a gel before the library prep.

steps.title: Pool and sequence
instructions: Pool each index plate on its own and clean the pool up.
notes: This read pools 2 plates. One axis of the address is the plate, so the marks tell 96 plates apart on one flow cell.
expected: Reads for 128 wells, every well told from the rest by the marks it carries.

steps.title: Call every well
instructions: Demultiplex the reads by address, checking each address rather than trusting a file.
Call a consensus a well, then compare it with that well's design base for base.
Reformat, compacting out the wells that failed.
notes: A well read too thinly carries no verdict and is not a failure, so reformatting does not compact it out.
More than one consensus is mixed, and mixed fails.
A design with no passing well is picked again from the same archive spot before anyone re-synthesises it.
expected: A well read more than 20 times is called; the index PCR route tolerates 10 reads and warns between the two.
A pass matches across the whole designed region: both entry overhangs, the fragment, the stuffer and the barcode.

troubleshooting.problem: A well's call is the right protein and the wrong barcode
troubleshooting.solution: It fails. A barcode that no longer names its member cannot be put right by the linkage read later.
